title: Phased Trajectory Ops Lane & SLO Scorecard
body:
Purpose:
This working brief defines a phased roadmap lane for product rollouts tied directly to operational KPIs and SLOs. The goal is a compact, actionable scorecard product teams and oncall can use during progressive traffic ramps across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This doc is intentionally operational (runbook-adjacent) — not a strategic roadmap.

Context / why this is different:
- Many existing checklists focus on go/no-go day-of launch; this doc ties release phases to explicit SLO headroom, cost-per-token thresholds, and rollback windows so rollouts can be controlled by measurable system and business signals.
- Includes specific tests for Dedicated and Private topologies (network egress, KMS latencies, and on-prem node drain tests) that are often missing from generic launch lists.

Summary of phases (short form):
- Phase 0: Canary smoke (0.1% traffic) — validate infra, function hooks, billing meters.
- Phase 1: Micro ramp (1-2% traffic) — KPI gating: p50 latency, error-rate, unit-cost.
- Phase 2: Pace-up (5-15% traffic) — SLO validation under sustained load, KV cache warmers, batching efficiency checks.
- Phase 3: Broad ramp (25-50% traffic) — economy controls (quant profiles, fallback models), start autoscale schedule for Dedicated pools.
- Phase 4: Steady state (>50%) — monitoring only, weekly quality regressions and cost audits.

Scorecard (per-phase):
- For each phase track: start_time, duration_target, owner, pass/fail signals, required approvals, rollback window.
- Minimum pass signals (must all be green to proceed):
  * p50 latency <= phase threshold (ms)
  * p95 latency <= phase threshold (ms)
  * error rate (5xx + client errors) < 0.5%
  * token-level cost delta vs baseline <= +20% (Phase 1), +10% (Phase 2+)
  * Quality regression alert rate = 0 (no new eval failures on critical prompt set)

Operational KPIs (tracked continuously):
- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 broken out by model and route.
- Availability: successful requests% (SLO target 99.95% for Hosted, 99.9% for Dedicated initial)
- Unit economics: cost per 1k tokens by model variant and quantization level.
- Cache hit ratio: prefix/KV cache % — aim > 60% for chat-heavy workloads.
- Autoscale churn: number of scale events per hour (goal < 6 during steady traffic).
- Eval quality metrics: prompt set pass-rate and regression count.

Phase gating thresholds (examples):
- Phase 0 -> 1: p95 < 600ms, errors < 1%, billing pipeline validated, smoke tests pass 
- Phase 1 -> 2: p95 < 400ms, errors < 0.8%, unit-cost delta <= +20%, canary eval set pass-rate >= 98%
- Phase 2 -> 3: p95 < 300ms, errors < 0.5%, autoscale stable for 60m, cache hit > 50%
- Phase 3 -> 4: p95 < 250ms, errors < 0.3%, unit-cost delta <= +10%, SLAs matched in target regions

Runbook snippets (quick actionable checks before moving phase):
- Pre-move checklist (15–30m before):
  1) Confirm metric ingestion for all KPIs (Datadog dashboards live, alerting active)
  2) Validate billing reports for canary requests — cost tags present
  3) Confirm model pin/version and fallback mapping (rollforward/rollback map documented)
  4) Notify oncall with expected move timestamp and SLAs to watch (channel + pinned message)
  5) Ensure warmers run for 5m on top 10 routes (if applicable)

- Immediate post-move checks (0–15m):
  * p50/p95 trending in dashboards, no spike in 5xx or throttles
  * QPS and batch sizes within expected distribution
  * No new client-side validation failures in ingestion pipeline

Test matrix (examples to run during Phase 1-2):
- Functional: core API happy-path, function/tool-calling contract tests, structured-output parser tests
- Load: 5m sustained at expected phase qps, 3x spike tests to check autoscale behavior
- Latency sensitivity: synthetic traces with long-context prompts to validate KV eviction behavior
- Network/security: TLS renegotiation, KMS latency sampling (for Private/VPC), egress route failover test (Dedicated)

Dedicated/Private-specific checks (must be green for those deployments):
- KMS roundtrip median latency < 80ms for decrypt ops on cold path
- Audit log delivery validated end-to-end (customer syslog endpoint test)
- Node drain test: simulate unavailable GPU node and validate graceful failover in < 45s
- VPC egress failover: route to backup region and confirm no auth regressions

Communication & approvals:
- Approvals required per phase: product-ops owner + eng oncall + SRE lead. For Dedicated/Private add solutions engineering approval.
- Notification template (Slack): short header with phase move time, expected traffic %, owners, key KPIs to monitor, rollback trigger summary and link to runbook.

Rollback triggers (automated + manual):
- Automated rollback (immediate): sustained error-rate > 1.5% for 3m OR p95 exceeds phase threshold by > 2x for 2m
- Manual rollback (operator discretion): any critical eval regression flagged by canary prompts, billing anomaly (>50% cost increase vs baseline), or customer-reported functional failure in production

Post-mortem and learning capture:
- If rollback happens, capture: timestamp, top-3 metric deltas, timeline of escalation, root cause hypothesis, and three recommended mitigations. Put summary in Confluence and tag the rollout ticket.
- Weekly post-rollout audit for first 2 weeks: cost delta, quality regressions, latency drift, autoscale events.

Suggested dashboard layout (quick):
- Top row: live traffic %, active model variant, overall success %
- Middle row: latency heatmaps by route & model, unit-cost sparkline, cache hit %
- Bottom row: eval pass-rate, autoscale events timeline, error breakdown by code

Open questions / TODO (notes to self):
- Decide canonical prompt set for early-eval (Maya to propose sample set + owner)
- Add an automated cost tagging policy for Private deployments (billing team dependency)
- Document model-variant compatibility matrix for fallback during capacity constraints

Related artifacts and references:
- See CONFLUENCE-4821 for canonical rollout ticket template
- See JIRA-OPS-1187 for recent Dedicated node-drain incident notes
- Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood/rollouts/pull/62 (auto-gate tooling prototype)

Quick contact list (phone/email left out; Slack handles recommended):
- Product Ops: @ava.chen (owner)
- Serving Runtime Eng: @ravi.patel (eng lead)
- SRE: @jordan_ng (oncall)

Notes (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally tight. If we need broader playbooks, extract into playbook repo and add links here.
- I expect the first run to be messy — iterate after two rollouts and lock the metric thresholds then.
